title: Sydney CBD and Kings Cross lockout and last-drinks laws (NSW)
summary: The Liquor Amendment Act 2014 created the Sydney CBD Entertainment Precinct and imposed 1.30am lockouts and 3am last drinks there and in Kings Cross, a freeze on new liquor licences in the precinct, risk-based licence fees and a statewide 10pm takeaway cut-off.

instruments.title: Liquor Amendment Act 2014 No 3
instruments.provisions: Amends Liquor Act 2007; ss 116G-116H commenced 15 Mar 2014 (2014 No 110)

commenced.what: 1.30am lockout and 3am last drinks began in the CBD Entertainment Precinct and Kings Cross; 10pm takeaway limit statewide

direction_rationale: Trading-hour restrictions and a freeze on new licences in the precinct cap entry and reduce the ability of late-night venues to compete, likely protecting incumbent licences and shifting activity to other areas.
comparison: Venues outside the precincts in Sydney; other capital cities; spatial (SA2) comparisons for licence data
confounders: 2016 Callinan review relaxations for live-entertainment venues
Statewide takeaway restriction affects all of NSW
notes: Precinct-level treatment is sub-state; state-level CABEE will dilute effects; use as heterogeneity with NSW liquor licence data.

verified.notes: 24 Feb 2014 start of lockouts is from news/law-firm sources; the official instrument fixing that date was not identified.

assessment.summary: 1.30am lockouts, 3am last drinks and a freeze on new liquor licences in Sydney's CBD and Kings Cross, aimed at alcohol-related violence. Venues closed and activity moved elsewhere; the freeze shielded existing licences from new rivals.

marks.reason: A freeze on new liquor licences in the precinct blocks new venues.
Lockouts and earlier last drinks limit how late venues can trade and compete.

assessment.confidence_note: Safety benefits, the reason for the laws, are not weighed here.
